text: # BOEING 737 FLIGHT CREW OPERATING MANUAL ## STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURES — REVISION 4.0 DOCUMENT ID: SOP-OPS-737-04 EFFECTIVE DATE: 2024-01-15 SUPERSEDES: SOP-OPS-737-03 STATUS: CURRENT ### 1. STERILE FLIGHT DECK PROCEDURES Sterile flight deck procedures must be strictly observed during all critical phases of flight below 10,000 feet MSL (Mean Sea Level). Critical phases include all ground operations involving pushback, taxi, takeoff roll, initial climb through 10,000 feet, descent below 10,000 feet, approach, landing, and taxi to gate. During sterile cockpit periods: - No non-essential flight deck conversations, personal discussions, or jokes are permitted. - Reading material unrelated to flight operations (e.g. newspapers, personal mobile devices) is strictly prohibited. - Flight attendants shall not contact the flight deck via interphone unless an immediate safety or emergency condition exists (e.g., fire, smoke, cabin pressure anomaly, medical emergency). - Any flight crew member who observes non-essential distractions shall issue the mandatory callout: "STERILE COCKPIT". ### 2. CLIMB AND DESCENT VERIFICATION Upon climbing through 10,000 feet MSL, the Pilot Flying (PF) or Pilot Monitoring (PM) shall state: "10,000 FEET — STERILE COCKPIT TERMINATED". Recognition lights and landing lights may be turned OFF at pilot discretion. Upon descending through 10,000 feet MSL, the Pilot Monitoring shall call out: "10,000 FEET — STERILE COCKPIT IN EFFECT", and illuminate landing lights and fasten seatbelt signs.

text: # BOEING 737 FLIGHT CREW OPERATING MANUAL ## STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURES — REVISION 3.0 DOCUMENT ID: SOP-OPS-737-03 EFFECTIVE DATE: 2021-06-01 STATUS: SUPERSEDED ### 1. STERILE FLIGHT DECK PROCEDURES Sterile flight deck procedures must be maintained during all critical phases of flight below 8,000 feet MSL. Non-operational conversation is prohibited during takeoff roll, initial climb through 8,000 feet, and final approach. During sterile cockpit periods: - Casual flight deck conversations are prohibited below 8,000 feet. - Flight attendants should minimize calls to the cockpit during takeoff and landing. - The 8,000 feet altitude was previously deemed sufficient for terminal airspace transitions under 2021 fleet rules. ### 2. CLIMB AND DESCENT CALLOUTS At 8,000 feet MSL on departure, the PM calls "8,000 FEET". Sterile cockpit rules terminate. On descent through 8,000 feet MSL, PM calls "8,000 FEET". Sterile cockpit begins.

text: # QUICK REFERENCE HANDBOOK (QRH) ## EMERGENCY PROCEDURES — BOEING 737 FLEET DOCUMENT ID: QRH-EMER-01 VERSION: 2.1 EFFECTIVE DATE: 2023-09-01 STATUS: CURRENT ### EMERGENCY DESCENT CHECKLIST Condition: Rapid cabin depressurization or catastrophic loss of cabin pressure at altitude. #### Immediate Action Items (Memory Items): 1. **OXYGEN MASKS AND REGULATORS**: DON 100% EMERGENCY FLOW (Both Pilots). 2. **CREW COMMUNICATIONS**: ESTABLISH via flight interphone. 3. **PASSENGER OXYGEN SWITCH**: ON (Deploy passenger masks if cabin altitude exceeds 14,000 feet). 4. **THRUST LEVERS**: CLOSE TO IDLE. 5. **AUTOTHROTTLE**: DISENGAGE. 6. **SPEEDBRAKE LEVER**: EXTEND FULLY. 7. **DESCENT TARGET ALTITUDE**: Set MCP altitude window to 10,000 FEET or Minimum Off-Route Altitude (MORA), whichever is higher. 8. **AIRSPEED**: Maintain Vmo/Mmo (Maximum Operating Speed) unless structural damage is suspected. If structural turbulence or airframe damage is suspected, maintain 250 KIAS. 9. **TRANSPONDER**: SQUAWK 7700. 10. **ATC NOTIFICATION**: Declare "MAYDAY, MAYDAY, MAYDAY - EMERGENCY DESCENT IN PROGRESS". Level Off Procedure: - At 2,000 feet above target altitude: Smoothly retract speedbrakes. - At 1,000 feet above target altitude: Advance thrust levers to maintain 250 knots. - Once leveled at 10,000 feet or MEA: Check cabin altitude; remove flight crew oxygen masks when cabin altitude is verified below 10,000 feet.

text: FLIGHT OPERATIONS SAFETY BULLETIN BULLETIN NO: OPS-BUL-2024-08 SUBJECT: Severe Turbulence Penetration Procedures and Airspeed Targets EFFECTIVE DATE: 2024-03-20 STATUS: CURRENT APPLICABILITY: All Commercial Jet Fleet (B737, B777, A320) 1. TURBULENCE PENETRATION AIRSPEED LIMITS When penetrating severe clear-air turbulence (CAT) or convective mountain wave activity, pilots must adhere strictly to recommended target speeds. Do NOT chase indicated airspeed fluctuations on the Primary Flight Display. Target Airspeed: Maintain 280 KIAS or 0.76 Mach, whichever is lower. Pitch Attitude: Fly attitude control with reference to the Artificial Horizon / Attitude Indicator. Allow airspeed and altitude to vary; excessive control inputs may overstress flight controls and airframe structures. Engine Ignition: Switch engine start switches to CONT (Continuous) or FLT to protect against engine flameout from compressor stalls. Autopilot / Autothrottle: Disengage Autothrottle. Disengage Autopilot Altitude Hold (ALT HLD) mode to avoid aggressive pitch corrections during updrafts or downdrafts. Heading Select (HDG SEL) and basic Attitude Hold may remain engaged. 2. CABIN SAFETY DIRECTIVES Immediate actions upon encountering moderate or severe turbulence: Turn FASTEN SEAT BELT signs ON. Make mandatory PA announcement: "FLIGHT ATTENDANTS BE SEATED IMMEDIATELY". Suspend all cabin service, hot beverage distribution, and secure galley carts.

text: # FEDERAL AVIATION ADMINISTRATION REGULATORY DIRECTIVE ## 14 CFR PART 121.639 — FUEL REQUIREMENTS FOR DOMESTIC IFR FLIGHTS DOCUMENT ID: FAR-PART-121-639 VERSION: REG-2023.1 EFFECTIVE DATE: 2023-01-01 STATUS: CURRENT DOCUMENT TYPE: Regulatory Directive ### 1. GENERAL DOMESTIC DISPATCH FUEL RESERVES No person may dispatch or take off an airplane in domestic air carrier operations unless it carries enough fuel: (a) To fly to the airport to which it is dispatched (Trip Fuel); (b) Thereafter, to fly to and land at the most distant alternate airport specified in the dispatch release (Alternate Fuel); and (c) Thereafter, to fly for 45 minutes at normal cruising fuel consumption rate (Reserve Fuel). ### 2. DISPATCH CONTINGENCY FUEL When destination weather indicates adverse conditions, convective SIGMETs, or expected air traffic holding delays: - Dispatchers must add minimum 15 minutes of contingency fuel. - In terminal areas with Ground Delay Programs (GDP), required expected delay fuel must be loaded in addition to the 45-minute statutory reserve. - Flight crew may not accept a dispatch release if the planned fuel at touchdown is less than the 45-minute FAR reserve requirement.

text: # AIRLINE GROUND OPERATIONS MANUAL ## STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURES — WINTER DE-ICING DOCUMENT ID: SOP-WINTER-OPS-2022 VERSION: WIN-2022.2 EFFECTIVE DATE: 2022-11-01 EXPIRY DATE: 2023-04-30 STATUS: EXPIRED DOCUMENT TYPE: Standard Operating Procedure ### 1. HOLDOVER TIMES (HOT) FOR TYPE I AND TYPE IV FLUIDS Caution: This procedure expired on 2023-04-30. Revised seasonal holdover tables are published annually by Flight Operations Engineering. Holdover table guidelines: - Type I fluid (50/50 mix heated at 60C): Active frost at -3C to 0C provides 45 minutes holdover protection. - Freezing fog at -4C: Type I fluid provides 11 to 17 minutes holdover protection. - Type IV anti-icing fluid: Active snow provides 35 to 75 minutes holdover time depending on precipitation intensity. ### 2. PRE-TAKEOFF CONTAMINATION CHECK If holdover time expires prior to takeoff: - Flight crew must request a secondary de-icing spray or perform a pre-takeoff contamination inspection from the cabin windows within 5 minutes of takeoff roll. - If wing contamination (snow, frost, or slush) is visually detected on upper wing surfaces or control tabs, takeoff is strictly prohibited until a complete de-icing cycle is repeated.
